title: Tenant ops briefing: upgrade announcement frames + terraform quicknotes
content:
Purpose:
This working draft collects short customer-facing announcement templates, an internal briefing checklist, a tenant impact matrix, and lightweight Terraform module notes we can drop into release PRs for private (VPC/on-prem) upgrades. Goal: create a single, copy-paste-ready set of messages and ops hints so Solutions/CS/SEs and SRE can coordinate cleanly with minimum back-and-forth.

Summary for quick copy:
- Audience: private deployment customers (VPC and on-prem packages)
- Scope: minor patch / minor version upgrade / data-plane kernel update (we include separate frames)
- Expectation: most upgrades are rolling with no data loss; customers may see 1–3% increased latency for short windows, or brief connection resets if tenant networking path cicrulates.

1) Short email announcement (72h before, generic):
Subject: Scheduled maintenance: Redwood platform update for {{TENANT_NAME}} on {{DATE}}
Hello {{TENANT_ADMIN}},
We will perform a planned update to your Redwood deployment in {{REGION}} on {{DATE}} between {{START_TIME}} and {{END_TIME}} (local time). This update installs a minor performance and reliability patch. During the window you may see short request retries or marginally higher latency for up to 20 minutes per upgrade wave.
What we do: rolling upgrade of inference nodes (no data-plane schema changes).
Action for you: no action required unless you rely on pinned kernel behavior — if so, reply to this thread.
Rollback: we will rollback automatically if we detect increased error rates or SLO violations above thresholds defined in your SLA.
Contact: redwood-support+{{TENANT_ID}}@redwood.ai (for urgent impact, escalate to oncall SRE: pager ID: {{PAGER_ID}}).
Thanks,
Redwood Private Deployments Team

2) Short Slack message (24h before):
Hey {{TENANT_TEAM}} — Reminder: rolling infra upgrade tomorrow {{DATE}} {{START_TIME}}–{{END_TIME}}. Expect brief connection resets in < 5% of requests during waves. Questions: ping @sre-private or reply to this thread.

3) Urgent outage frame (postmortem-style, 1-line to customers):
Subject: Incident update: service disruption during maintenance on {{DATE}}
We observed an unexpected failure during the upgrade that caused increased error rates between {{TIME_A}} and {{TIME_B}}. Root cause: kernel transition race in the GPU runtime; mitigation: rollback to previous variant and re-run patch with staggered waves. Full postmortem to follow.

4) Tenant impact matrix (quick reference for comms tone):
- Impact Level 0: No user-visible effect. Use one-line heads-up.
- Impact Level 1: Transient latency/retry (<=1 minute). Use 72h + 24h reminders.
- Impact Level 2: Repeated retries / short errors (1–20 minutes). Use 72h + immediate pre-window + live Slack channel + escalation list.
- Impact Level 3: Partial outage (>20 minutes or data loss risk). Declare incident, invoke incident response, offer extended runbook + credits per SLA.

5) Internal briefing checklist (ops runbook excerpt):
- Pre-cutover (T-7d): Verify Terraform plan for target tenant modules; ensure module versions pinned in upgrade PR; validate CI e2e smoke tests on staging tenant.
- T-72h: Send 72h announcement email.
- T-24h: Confirm provisioning quotas and GPU pool headroom. Post Slack reminder.
- T-1h: Warm caches; lock rollout policy to 10% wave.
- During: Monitor error-rate, latency p95/p99, queue-backlog. If error-rate > 3x baseline AND sustained for > 2 minutes, trigger automated rollback.
- Post: Run validation prompt set (10 representative prompts) and check model hash and KV cache health.

6) Quick Terraform module notes (for PRs and inline comments):
- Purpose: when we upgrade serving runtime or inference kernels we also sometimes need to bump the terraform module that annotates allowed kernel profiles for a tenant cluster. Keep notes short and actionable.
- Example annotation to include in upgrade PR description: "tf-annotation: module=tenant-cluster v=3.2.1 -> v=3.2.2; requires node-pool-dual-kernel flag; plan shows 0->2 instance replacements"
- Minimal snippet to add in module root (example, for reviewers):
resource "redwood_infra_node_pool" "tenant_nodes" {
  name = var.name
  version = "3.2.2" # bumped for kernel stabilization
  lifecycle_replace_on_version = true
}
Notes: lifecycle_replace_on_version flips causing rolling replacements; confirm cluster-level evictionPolicy=graceful to avoid request drops.

7) Rollback/validation quick commands (ops notes):
- Validate model runtime after wave: curl -X POST https://{{TENANT_ENDPOINT}}/v1/healthz 
  expect {"runtime":"ok", "model_hash":"{{EXPECTED_HASH}}"}
- Forced rollback via TF: comment on PR with "rollback=true" triggers automation. Manual: terraform apply -var "force_version={{OLD_VERSION}}" -auto-approve

8) Customer-facing FAQ snippets (short answers to predictable questions):
Q: Will my data be migrated or changed?
A: No schema or data migration is included in minor kernel/patch upgrades. All customer data and prompts remain intact.
Q: Will this change model outputs?
A: No. We only apply runtime/latency patches; if model weights change we will notify separately and offer a canary window.

9) TODOs and open questions (for the team):
- [ ] Add localized timezone helper snippets for EMEA/APAC comms.
- [ ] Decide deadline for pinning module versions 48h before rollout. (proposal: T-72h).
- [ ] Draft a short one-click tenant consent checkbox flow for minor upgrades.

10) Back-of-envelope SLO impact language (for legal/comms):
If upgrade causes an SLO breach for a tenant (error rate > 0.5% for > 1 hour), we will follow SLA credit rules documented in the tenant contract. For communications, use the Impact Level 2 template and offer a post-incident remediation plan.

11) Quick paste bank (small snippets for CS/SEs):
- Opening line for low-impact: "We plan a rolling maintenance that is unlikely to affect your traffic. Expect transient retries for up to a few minutes per node wave."
- Opening line for medium-impact: "During the upgrade you may see intermittent increased latency and a small number of failed requests. We will be monitoring closely and can roll back immediately."

Notes to reviewer: keep language conservative for public-facing templates (avoid promising "no impact"). The document is intentionally terse; copy and paste sections into customer replies or PR descriptions.

Revision history: v0.1 initial draft (2025-01-12) by Priya; v0.2 added TF snippet and impact matrix (2025-01-19 Marco); v0.3 added rollback commands and FAQ (2025-02-03 Ada).

END
